answers.answer: `plan-json history` accepts an optional positional `req`, but `dispatch` rejects any non-None value with status 2 before checking `--force` or `--kind`. With no REQ, it then rejects `--force`, then missing `--kind`, and otherwise calls `project_history`; producer input errors are also returned as status 2. The CLI test asserts that history needs `--kind` and other actions need a REQ.

Accepted kinds are `implement`, `test`, `docs`, `audit`, and `research`. Context fields are `complexity` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `extreme`), `scope` (`isolated_fix`, `small_change`, `large_change`, `full_feature`, `full_system`), and `risk`/`coupling` (`low`, `medium`, `high`). Omitted dimensions are returned as `null`. Unknown context keys, non-string keys, non-mapping context, invalid values, and invalid kinds raise redacted `PlanningHistoryInputError`s; CLI `choices` also reject unsupported values during argument parsing.

The result includes four metrics, all with `status` and `source_quality` set to `unknown`, a null `comparability_key`, and a reason. Quality has `samples`, `successes`, `failures`, `observed_rate`, and `uncertainty_interval_95` all null. Duration has null `samples`, `median`, and `range`, with unit `seconds`. Retries has null `samples` and `count`. Consumption has null `samples`, `unit`, `median`, `range`, and `coverage`. These are schema placeholders, not observed numbers.

The history projection directly constructs unknown metrics; its caller passes only kind and normalized context, and it does not load or aggregate telemetry. Nearby M2 route snapshots are keyed by provider/model/profile/effort/kind and wired into route candidates. A separate M2 performance-history aggregator requires a route ID, correlated eligible outcomes, and context data. Attempt rows expose route and duration/token details, but the projection’s stated rationale is that attempts are not correlated to applied M6 outcomes and token units differ across providers. Those route-scoped or differently correlated inputs therefore do not automatically become this cross-route projection’s measurements.

The tests assert that all projection metrics remain unknown with null measurements, and recursively check serialized output for the keys `route`, `route_id`, `provider`, `model`, `account`, `effort`, and `quota`. They also assert the report can be JSON-serialized. These source assertions do not measure live performance, inspect live telemetry, or establish whether any route has enough observed samples.
